context:
Not urgent. Your want (chat, 15:08 CDT): set a context limit per kind of session, not only per model, for example a different limit for orchestrators on Opus 5.5 than for the coordinator. "Context limit" here means how much of a conversation a session holds before it condenses its history (compaction).

What a docs check found (code.claude.com/docs: model-config, settings, sub-agents, env-vars):
- Sessions on your own computer: yes. Each launch can set its own window with `claude --autocompact <tokens>` or `--settings '{"autoCompactWindow": N}'`. Nothing raises a window above the model's own cap.
- Helper agents: an agent file's setting `autoCompactWindow` (100000 to 1000000) lowers the window for that kind of agent.
- The environment variable `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` overrides all of the above, so it must stay out of shared environment files.
- Cloud sessions (the kind these sessions run in): no documented per-session setting. The likely route is one cloud environment per kind of session, each with its own `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW`. A coordinator can already start a session in a chosen environment, so lanes could start in a "lane" environment. That is an inference, not in the docs, and untested.

Your measurement (chat, 15:20 CDT): once claude-settings was installed, cloud sessions moved from a 1M window to the 500k that its settings.json sets (`autoCompactWindow: 500000`, line 433 on main). So the repo's settings already reach cloud sessions, which makes the one-environment-per-kind route more plausible. It is still not proven for a different number per kind.

options.gain: A real answer for cloud sessions, which is where most lanes run.
options.how:
You make one extra cloud environment with the variable set to a lower number. A coordinator starts a lane session in it, and we check that it condenses at that number.
Before: all cloud sessions share one limit. After: you know whether a lane environment can have its own.
options.label: Test the cloud route
options.lose: One extra environment for you to make and keep, and one test session.

options.gain: No test and no new environment; uses what is documented.
options.how:
Set limits only where the docs document them: on each local launch and in each agent file. Do nothing for cloud sessions.
Before: one limit everywhere. After: tiers on your computer and helper agents can differ; cloud sessions stay as they are.
options.label: Local sessions and agent files only
options.lose: Cloud sessions cannot have a different limit per kind.

options.gain: Nothing to build or keep up.
options.how:
No change; every session keeps its model's default limit.
Before and after: the same.
options.label: Drop the want
options.lose: You cannot tune cost or memory per kind of session.

title: Can each kind of session get its own context limit? Test it for cloud sessions?
why: Most lanes run in the cloud, so the cloud answer is the one that matters, and one test settles what the docs leave open.
